job_2_the_tripwire_was_hoisted_over.what_was_wrong: Round 2 took its before-fingerprint inside `main()`. ESM evaluates every `import` before the importing module's body, so a static top-level `import './gen-greetings.mjs'` ran, rewrote `greetings.json`, and THEN the fingerprint was taken — of the damage. The round-2 critic measured exit 0 printing PASS with the leak deleted.
job_2_the_tripwire_was_hoisted_over.hazards_31s_own_stated_fix_is_necessary_: §31 says 'take the fingerprint at MODULE SCOPE, before any import can run'. Module scope is still the importer's body, which still runs after ALL of its imports — so that alone does not fix it. The only hook ESM offers that runs before another module's body is BEING an earlier module in the import list. `tools/lib/evidence-seal.mjs` takes the hash in its OWN module body and the invariant is mechanical: it must be the FIRST import statement in any check that uses it.
both_ways_of_defeating_it_are_closed: generator imported AFTER the seal -> the seal was already taken -> hashes differ -> exit 4
generator imported BEFORE the seal -> `verifySeal()` re-reads the caller's own source, strips comments, resolves the first import statement, and fails because it is not the seal -> exit 4

ruling_NOT_THIS_ROUND_and_why: IT IS NOT A TOKEN SUBSTITUTION. RI-DLG03 §C requires *distinct greeting entries, cell-filtered to the settlement* — 30/24/12/8 by tier, with 5/5/4/3 disposition bands each and a per-band minimum. Across 8 settlements that is on the order of 120-200 NEW distinct authored greetings, not a `{town}` placeholder. A mail-merged town name would satisfy the regex in step 2 and satisfy nothing else, and Morrowind's greetings are cell-FILTERED, not cell-templated.

IT MOVES THE FLOOR UNDER THIS ROUND'S GUARDS. A settlement key changes the pool schema, the 300-cell contract in `gen-greetings.mjs`, `check-greeting-voice.mjs`'s address derivation (which depends on 5 bands per (group, class) agreeing) and `check-composed-greetings.mjs`'s cell->class resolution.
